drivers.evidence: DXY’s Friday last trade was 103.840 versus Thursday’s provider close of 103.900. The small decline eases the currency cost of gold for non-dollar buyers. This closed-market observation is stale on Sunday.

Treasury’s 20 Nov 10-year real yield fell 11bp to 2.77%; the nominal yield fell 12bp to 4.92%. Lower after-inflation bond income reduces gold’s opportunity cost. These are Friday observations, not fresh Sunday moves.

Investing.com’s 21 Nov 13:35 HKT update puts December’s hold probability at 13.6%, versus zero in the previous edition. January’s cumulative half-point outcome fell to 51.5% from 70.0%. Less tightening reduces the expected interest advantage of cash over gold; these weekend-displayed probabilities are stale.

Kitco reported Friday cross-asset liquidation as metals fell with stocks. That selling channel pressures gold despite stress that may attract haven demand. AP reports at least three tankers attacked around Hormuz on Saturday; no post-attack gold or oil price is available while markets are closed.
drivers.why: Liquidation is bearish for gold; equity stress and shipping attacks may support haven demand. No reopened-market response confirms the latter channel.

drivers.evidence: The issuer archive reaches 19 Nov: GLD held 1,038.14 tonnes, down 5.98 tonnes from 18 Nov. gold.competing: Lower real yields, a slightly weaker dollar and less tightening priced in would normally help gold. They failed to prevent Friday’s fall. Reported liquidation is a competing explanation, while fresh shipping attacks add weekend uncertainty without a tradable gold response yet. The conflict keeps evidence confidence Low.
gold.would_change: After this window, US October PCE and second-estimate Q3 GDP arrive Wednesday 25 Nov at 21:30 HKT. Persistent inflation or weaker real growth would change the balance.

ai_stories.paragraph: A mathematical proof must connect its starting assumptions to its conclusion through valid logical steps. A computer can check those steps when they are written in a precise language. Levent Alpöge announced a Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis, which concerns the distribution of prime numbers, on November 20. He released it as Lean code. On November 21, the Lean and Mathlib communities certified both the theorem statement and the proof. Independent tools matched the statement against the established version, and multiple checkers accepted the proof. Mathematicians still have work to do explaining its new ideas so people can understand how the argument succeeds.
ai_stories.headline: Independent checkers endorse a Claude-assisted Riemann proof
facts: On 20 November 2026 mathematician Levent Alpöge announced a proof of the Riemann hypothesis developed with Claude, released as Lean code rather than a conventional paper.
The Riemann hypothesis concerns how prime numbers are distributed.
On 21 November the Lean and Mathlib communities issued a joint statement endorsed by Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative, certifying the correct theorem statement and proof.
The statement says the code compiled, two independent tools matched it against Mathlib's established Riemann statement, and multiple proof checkers accepted an inert proof export.
The community says mathematical work remains to explain the proof's new ideas. Machine checking the stated theorem is distinct from humans understanding the argument.

ai_stories.paragraph: An AI model processes text through a sequence of calculation layers. Thinking Machines Lab’s Inkling 2 Mini runs its middle layers three times for each piece of output, like working through the same worksheet several times before answering. Reusing the layers avoids storing three separate copies. Released with open weights on November 20, it has 26.4 billion parameters and uses roughly 20GB of memory. Running it locally on a Mac requires at least 32GB of memory at launch. Its developer says repeated passes improve reasoning efficiency, while stored factual knowledge remains limited by model size. Performance across real tasks remains an open question.
ai_stories.headline: A smaller model reuses its middle layers
facts: Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Mini with open weights on 20 November 2026.
It runs its middle model layers three times per output token, reusing them rather than storing three separate copies.
The company reports 26.4 billion total parameters and a roughly 20GB memory footprint, with local Mac support requiring at least 32GB RAM at launch.
Its developer says repeated passes improve reasoning efficiency but do not add more stored factual knowledge; factual knowledge remains limited by model size.
Company benchmark claims are provider evaluations, not proof it performs best on every real task.

ai_stories.paragraph: A private message has to become readable on a screen before its recipient can read it. That creates another place where software could capture it, even when the message was protected during delivery. Signal announced screenshot blocking for iOS 27 on November 20, alongside protection on Android versions where it can detect AI assistants reading the screen. The aim is to stop operating-system AI agents accessing displayed conversations. Users can turn protection off to take screenshots, potentially exposing messages. Signal says coverage remains incomplete, with file access still possible, some Android devices uncovered and reliable screenshot blocking unavailable on macOS.
ai_stories.headline: Signal blocks more AI screen capture
facts: Signal's 20 November 2026 post announces screenshot blocking on iOS 27 and protection on Android versions where it can detect AI assistants reading the screen.
The goal is to restrict operating-system AI agents from capturing, storing or accessing decrypted message content.
End-to-end encryption protects messages in transit but does not prevent an operating system capturing text displayed on a device.
Users can disable the protection to regain screenshots, potentially exposing conversations to OS agents.
Signal says the remedy is incomplete: file-system access is not blocked, not all Android devices are covered, and reliable screenshot blocking is unavailable on macOS.

lens.mechanics: Prices rise when money and credit spent grow faster than output. Gold pays no income, so lower after-inflation bond returns usually improve its relative appeal.
lens.data: Three forces matter. First, the 20 Nov real yield fell to 2.77% from 2.88%, reducing that income disadvantage. Second, inflation compensation slipped to 2.15% from 2.16%. Third, claims were 203,000 for the week to 14 Nov, not a sudden labour collapse. Unlike the usual template, gold fell despite lower real yields. Reported liquidation is a possible missing force, not something these macro readings prove.
lens.unsustainable: Debt persistently outgrowing revenue requires adjustment through cuts, restructuring, transfers or monetary expansion.
lens.would_change: After this window, US October PCE and second-estimate Q3 GDP arrive Wednesday 25 Nov at 21:30 HKT. Persistent inflation or weaker real growth would change the balance.

longview.cycle: The checklist still suggests a highly indebted phase: debt grew relative to output and annual revenue, while foreign Treasury holdings grew more slowly than a year earlier. A household spending more income on interest has less room for other bills. The comparison has limits: the government issues its own currency, and these interest and revenue observations are from different quarters. Negative yield-growth gaps using one annualised quarter do not establish sustainable financing or predict a crisis date.
longview.asset_classes: Positive after-inflation Treasury yields compete with gold. Cash earns short-term interest and loses buying power if prices rise faster. If debt pressure leads to easing that cuts real returns, gold can gain through that channel. Bonds depend on inflation and repayment terms, while stocks depend on productivity and profits outrunning financing costs.
